s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory failure with mediastinal mass and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: Dyspnea on exertion and intermittent dry cough
Acute worsening of dyspnea leading to respiratory failure
Mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea
Pleural component with mass effect on surrounding structures
Lytic destruction of vertebrae and pneumomediastinum
key_facts: 1-month history of dyspnea on exertion and intermittent dry cough
Hyporexia and unquantified intermittent fever
Delayed care until acute worsening of dyspnea
Developed acute respiratory failure and pulseless electrical activity arrest
Required orotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation
Vital signs: blood pressure 200/140 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, respiratory rate 16 bpm, temperature 36 °C, oxygen saturation 78% on ventilatory support
Physical examination revealed anisocoria, jugular venous distension, sinus tachycardia, and bilateral coarse rales
Chest radiography showed homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass
Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
Laboratory tests showed WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL, hemoglobin 9.9 g/dL, platelets 303 × 10^3/µL, INR 1.39, lactic acid 2.83 mmol/L, C-reactive protein 4.20 mg/dL, LDH 592 U/L
Received dexamethasone and piperacillin/tazobactam
Video-assisted thoracoscopic biopsy planned to obtain adequate tissue

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and acute respiratory failure are consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Hodgkin lymphoma, Non-Hodgkin lymphoma can present with a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Thymoma is a type of tumor that can arise in the mediastinum and cause respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Thymic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Thymic carcinoma is a rare but aggressive tumor that can present with a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Mediastinal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal sarcoma is a rare tumor that can cause respiratory symptoms and a mediastinal mass

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis is a rare disease that can present with a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sarcoidosis is a disease that can cause a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms, although it is less likely given the acute presentation

shortlist.label: Germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Germ cell tumor is a type of tumor that can arise in the mediastinum and cause respiratory symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass, respiratory symptoms, and systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss, along with laboratory findings of elevated WBC, LDH, and C-reactive protein, is consistent with an aggressive lymphoma. The size and location of the mass, as well as the presence of a nodular pleural component, suggest an advanced stage of disease.

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: While possible, the large size and aggressive nature of the mass, as well as the lack of specific mention of Reed-Sternberg cells, make Non-Hodgkin lymphoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Thymoma
rejected.why: Thymomas are typically slower-growing and less likely to present with such a large mass and aggressive symptoms.

rejected.label: Thymic carcinoma
rejected.why: Thymic carcinomas are rare and aggressive, but the patient's presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with a lymphoma.

rejected.label: Mediastinal sarcoma
rejected.why: Sarcomas are rare in the mediastinum and would not typically present with such a large mass and systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: This is a rare condition that typically presents with pulmonary symptoms and skin lesions, which are not mentioned in the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis typically presents with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and pulmonary symptoms, but not a large mediastinal mass.

rejected.label: Germ cell tumor
rejected.why: Germ cell tumors are rare in the mediastinum and would not typically present with such a large mass and aggressive symptoms.
